goals: Validate ELM's runoff generation against observed streamflow at the American River gauge
Assess spatial heterogeneity in runoff contributions across the upstream basin

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM can generate spatially-distributed runoff (QOVER + QDRAI) across the upstream basin. Validation against a streamflow gauge requires aggregation + routing (not native to ELM).

answerable: Spatial pattern of runoff generation (QOVER + QDRAI) across elevation/soil/vegetation gradients
Elevation control on runoff timing via NLDAS-2 forcing (verified ~15 distinct precip values in 1625 m relief)
Soil texture control on infiltration and subsurface drainage
Vegetation control on ET and interception

not_answerable.aspect: Daily streamflow hydrograph at the gauge (m³/s)
not_answerable.why: ELM columns are independent 1-D points with no lateral transport or routing. Column runoff fluxes (mm/s) cannot be converted to gauge streamflow (m³/s) without spatial aggregation and routing.
not_answerable.needs: Runoff aggregation + routing capability (e.g. mizuRoute, RAPID)

not_answerable.why: NSE requires a modeled streamflow time series at the gauge, which depends on the aggregation + routing step above.

classes: fine (silt loam / clay loam, lower drainage)

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands × 2 soil classes × 2 vegetation types = 12 strata. Light replication (2 columns per stratum) = 24 total. This resolves the primary drivers of runoff generation (elevation/forcing, soil infiltration, vegetation ET) without over-sampling.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Distribute columns across the upstream basin of the American River gauge. Concentrate sampling in the mid-elevation rain-snow transition (900-1400 m) where runoff timing is most sensitive to temperature/precipitation phase. Ensure representation of dominant soil-vegetation combinations in each elevation band. Avoid ridgetops (unrepresentative of basin-average conditions) and focus on hillslopes and valley bottoms where runoff generation is strongest.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 columns per stratum to capture within-stratum variability and provide robustness against local anomalies (e.g. a single column hitting an unrepresentative soil patch).

sampling_plan.reason: Rain-dominated runoff, high infiltration, high ET — baseline low-elevation response
Rain-dominated, high infiltration, lower ET — tests vegetation control on low-elevation partitioning
Rain-dominated, lower infiltration, high ET — tests soil control on surface vs subsurface runoff
Rain-dominated, lower infiltration, lower ET — maximum low-elevation runoff generation
Rain-snow transition, high infiltration, high ET — critical for runoff timing (snowmelt + rain)
Rain-snow transition, high infiltration, lower ET — tests vegetation control on transition-zone partitioning
Rain-snow transition, lower infiltration, high ET — tests soil control on transition-zone runoff
Rain-snow transition, lower infiltration, lower ET — maximum transition-zone runoff generation
Snow-dominated, high infiltration, high ET — tests snowmelt-driven subsurface drainage
Snow-dominated, high infiltration, lower ET — tests vegetation control on high-elevation partitioning
Snow-dominated, lower infiltration, high ET — tests soil control on snowmelt runoff
Snow-dominated, lower infiltration, lower ET — maximum high-elevation runoff generation

validation_design.observation_source: USGS gauge: American River nr Nile
validation_design.comparison: aggregated — sum upstream column runoff (QOVER + QDRAI weighted by area), apply routing, compare to gauge
validation_design.n_validation_points: 0 co-located columns (gauge is a basin outlet, not a point source). Validation requires aggregation of all 24 upstream columns + routing.

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing (1980-2018), native SSURGO soil at each column location, WTD-informed warm start (Fan 2013 equilibrium water table)

requires_capabilities.capability: Upstream basin delineation for American River gauge
requires_capabilities.why: Need drainage area boundary to constrain column placement and aggregation
requires_capabilities.blocks: Cannot define the spatial domain for sampling or aggregation without the gauge's upstream basin

requires_capabilities.capability: Runoff aggregation (area-weighted sum of column QOVER + QDRAI)
requires_capabilities.why: ELM columns produce point fluxes (mm/s); must sum across upstream basin to get total runoff volume
requires_capabilities.blocks: Cannot convert column runoff to basin-scale runoff without aggregation

requires_capabilities.capability: Routing model (e.g. mizuRoute, RAPID, or simple lag function)
requires_capabilities.why: Aggregated runoff must be routed through the stream network to the gauge to account for travel time and attenuation
requires_capabilities.blocks: Cannot produce a streamflow hydrograph at the gauge without routing

requires_capabilities.capability: Gauge metadata (drainage area, exact lat/lon, record period)
requires_capabilities.why: Need drainage area for aggregation weighting, location for routing outlet, and record period to align validation window
requires_capabilities.blocks: Cannot verify data availability or align simulation period without metadata

requires_capabilities.why: Initialize subsurface storage realistically to avoid artifactually low QDRAI during validation period
requires_capabilities.blocks: Without warm start, subsurface drainage will be biased low (cold-start artifact), degrading streamflow validation

assumptions: The American River gauge drains a sub-basin within the Naches HUC8 (not the full HUC8 — exact boundary unknown)
NLDAS-2 forcing (1980-2018) covers the gauge's record period and is adequate for validation
The gauge record is daily and overlaps with 1980-2018 (not verified in brief)
Dominant soil and vegetation types can be sampled from SSURGO and land-cover datasets within the upstream basin
A WTD-informed warm start (Fan 2013) is available and preferred over multi-year spin-up
The 24-column sample is representative of the upstream basin's runoff generation (assumes the basin is not dominated by a single extreme condition outside the strata)
open_questions: What is the drainage area of the American River gauge? (needed for aggregation weighting)
What is the gauge's record period? (to align simulation and validation windows)
Is a routing model (mizuRoute, RAPID) available or planned? If not, can a simple area-weighted sum + lag function serve as a first-order approximation?
Are SSURGO soil and land-cover data available for the Naches basin to inform stratification?
Should the validation period be the full 1980-2018 or a subset (e.g. exclude drought/flood extremes for initial validation)?
